content: Horsehead Corporation was a U.S.-based industrial chemical and materials company headquartered at 300 Frankfort Road in Monaca, Pennsylvania (15061-2295). Founded in 1982 and formerly known as Horsehead Industries, the company specialized in the production of high-purity zinc metal and zinc-based products—most notably zinc oxide, zinc dust, and zinc powder—used across diverse sectors including rubber manufacturing, paints and coatings, agricultural micronutrients, pharmaceuticals, and battery technologies. Leveraging proprietary hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical processes, Horsehead differentiated itself through sustainable resource recovery, including the recycling of steel mill dust and other post-industrial residues to reclaim zinc and other valuable metals—effectively supporting circular economy principles. The Monaca facility, one of the largest integrated zinc recycling and refining operations in North America, served as both corporate headquarters and primary production site, employing advanced emission controls and energy recovery systems aligned with stringent EPA and Pennsylvania DEP environmental standards. Horsehead also operated complementary facilities in Texas and Tennessee, and maintained R&D capabilities focused on materials science innovations, especially in nanomaterials—though it did not manufacture or market “nan”-labeled products (e.g., “nan” in the address is a typographical artifact, not a reference to nanotechnology). The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in January 2016 and ceased operations later that year; its assets were subsequently acquired by American Zinc Recycling and later integrated into HZI (Horsehead Zinc, Inc.) under new ownership. While no longer active in its original form, Horsehead remains a notable case study in industrial recycling, metallurgical innovation, and the economic and regulatory challenges facing specialty chemical manufacturers in the 21st century.
